Numerical experiments confirm the fourth-order accuracy for a range of reaction-diffusion problems with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, and demonstrate that it outperforms existing standard ETD methods in serial and parallel implementations, yielding CPU time reductions of up to a factor of 20.

items.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
items.summary: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $δ_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

items.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
items.summary: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.

items.title: Shape Perturbation of the Galerkin Boundary Element Dirichlet-to-Neumann Matrix on Moving Polygons
items.summary: For nonlocal interface evolution problems such as the Mullins-Sekerka flow, certain parametric schemes discretize only the interface and approximate the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map by boundary elements. Their error analysis requires bounds on how this discrete operator changes as the polygon moves. In that analysis, the polygons are only Lipschitz and close to a smooth curve only in a Lipschitz norm, the perturbations are controlled only in the energy norm, and the kernels are singular on the diagonal. We study the symmetric Galerkin boundary element matrix on the polygons in a Lipschitz neighborhood of a smooth reference curve. Its first variation, tested against discrete Neumann solutions, is bounded by the energy norm of the perturbation alone. The second-order remainder of the associated mass form is bounded by the product of the energy norm and the Lipschitz norm of the perturbation, so that only one of the two factors needs a uniform bound. On the interpolating polygon, the matrix is consistent with the continuous operator without the logarithmic loss that a pointwise comparison of the kernels would suggest, and its shape derivative is consistent with that of the continuous operator. All bounds are uniform in the mesh size and depend only on the constants of the reference curve.

items.title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
items.summary: Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. We prove residualwise sharpness of the quadratic loss majorizer, monotonicity, compact containment, and stationarity of noncollapsed accumulation points. A uniform additive bound quantifies approximation to exact least-absolute conditional stress. The experiments use paired contamination, separately calibrated loss parameters, combined-configuration recovery, and direct checks of the theorem's inequalities.

items.title: Directed Singular-Value Sparsifiers with $O(n \log n/ε^2)$ Arcs
items.summary: Given an unweighted directed graph, a sparsifier is a nonnegative reweighting of original arcs that preserves every in-degree and out-degree exactly. In this work, we study singular-value sparsifiers, which are generalizations of spectral sparsifiers. Singular-value sparsifiers find a number of applications in theoretical computer science, such as maintaining directed cuts and flows, speeding up directed Laplacian solvers, and sparsifying dense weight matrices in neural networks. Strong singular-value (SV) approximation supports sparse representations of directed random walks with guarantees that remain stable under products, and controls bilinear error in the left and right Schur-complement metrics. We prove that every unweighted directed graph on $n$ vertices admits an $\varepsilon$-SV sparsifier with $O(n\log(2n)/\varepsilon^2)$ arcs, improving the $O(n\log^5 n/\varepsilon^2)$ support bound of Lau, Wang, and Zhou. The sparsifier is a nonnegative reweighting of original arcs and preserves every in-degree and out-degree exactly. We also give a randomized construction with $\tilde{O}(m+n)$ real-arithmetic running time, where $m$ is the input support size, and the output has the same support bound and rational weights of polynomial bit length.

items.title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
items.summary: This paper studies the numerical approximation of a mathematical model of coupled flow and viscoelastic deformation in a fractured porous medium including fracture contact mechanics. We consider a mixed-dimensional model, where the fracture is modeled as a co-dimension one object within the porous medium. This model couples Darcy flow in the matrix and fracture, linear viscoelasticity of the matrix and frictional contact mechanics of the fracture surfaces; the contact conditions include normal compliance and a Coulomb friction law. We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme for this problem, using conformal finite elements in space and the implicit Euler method in time. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution is established, and stability and a priori error estimates are derived. A numerical experiment is performed in which numerical error estimates are computed and compared to the theoretical results.

items.title: Pareto Front Tracing in Higher Dimensions Using Numerical Integration
items.summary: We propose a numerical integration approach for tracing the Pareto front of unconstrained continuous multi-objective optimization problems. By stating optimality conditions for weighted sum scalarizations, we derive parametric equations for Pareto critical points, parameterized by the weights. Sensitivity analysis with respect to the weights yields a system of partial differential equations (PDEs). We prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions and derive conditions under which a solution extends to the entire weight space and yields Pareto optimal solutions. A tracing strategy for the resulting PDE system is developed that uses numerical integration along individual weight coordinates using Runge--Kutta methods. We provide an error analysis considering inexact initial solutions, perturbations of the right-hand sides, and numerical integration errors. We investigate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the tracing strategy on convex quadratic problems and WFG examples, where the latter demonstrate the applicability to problems with Pareto fronts consisting of convex and non-convex parts. Comparisons with repeated weighted sum scalarizations and a predictor--corrector method illustrate the computational benefits of the proposed strategy.

items.title: Asymptotic Robustness of HDG Schemes for the Convection-Diffusion Equation
items.summary: The convection-diffusion problem has been studied extensively as an important model for convection-dominated problems. The problem becomes more challenging when the convecting velocity is no longer Lipschitz and merely has Sobolev regularity. In this paper, we use Boyer's extension of the DiPerna--Lions theory for the transport equation to study the vanishing diffusion limit of discretizations of the convection-diffusion equation with Sobolev velocity. In the case of flux-adapted boundary conditions, we prove that a continuous Galerkin discretization converges strongly to the renormalized solution of the transport equation as the diffusion coefficient and mesh size go to zero, without requiring any relationship between them. We refer to this unconditional strong convergence as asymptotic robustness. In the case of Dirichlet boundary conditions, we use the renormalization theory and barrier arguments to prove that a piecewise constant hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin scheme is asymptotically robust, while the continuous Galerkin scheme may fail to converge. Our results indicate that the asymptotic robustness of schemes for the convection-diffusion problem depends on the realization of the boundary conditions as opposed to internal layers.

items.title: Bounding and Approximating Kostka Numbers
items.summary: Kostka numbers, the coefficients of Schur polynomials, count semistandard Young tableaux of prescribed shape and weight. We give a deterministic algorithm for approximating Kostka numbers within a simply exponential factor in the number of variables and the size of the partition. Our approach combines Gurvits capacity bounds for log-concave polynomials with an algorithm for approximating the Gurvits capacity of a Schur polynomial. For a Schur polynomial in $n$ variables indexed by $λ$, we show that the logarithm of the capacity associated with any nonzero coefficient can be approximated to additive error $ε$ in time polynomial in $n$, $|λ|$, and $\log(1/ε)$. The analysis establishes an explicit bounded optimization region and efficient approximate first-order oracles, and handles boundary weights through a factorization into smaller Schur polynomials.

items.title: A New Computational Model for the Spin-Free Sum-of-Squares Energy Bounds of Electronic Hamiltonian
items.summary: Optimizing spin-free sum-of-squares (SOS) energy bounds for electronic Hamiltonians leads to semidefinite programs whose expanded size grows rapidly with the orbital dimension. We derive an exact reformulation of an established spin-free SOS model as a convex quadratic problem over a single symmetric matrix constrained between zero and the identity. Explicit recovery maps connect feasible quadratic-program iterates to certificates in the original SOS formulation, and identify the Frank--Wolfe gap with the separation between recovered primal and dual objectives. We implement the quadratic action through GPU-accelerated Coulomb contractions and solve the reformulated problem using a cached implementation of fully corrective Frank--Wolfe, referred to here as the dimension-reduced simplicial method (DRSM) that caches operator products and optimizes convex-combination weights in a small corrective quadratic program. Numerical experiments cover 65 FCIDUMP models, molecular geometries, and regular hydrogen rings, including original-coordinate recovery checks on nine instances and comparisons with FISTA and a boundary-point SDP solver. On eight H100 GPUs, a cold-start calculation for C$_{720}$ with 10,080 spatial orbitals reaches a freshly recomputed Frank--Wolfe gap of $8.82\times10^{-9}$ hartree in 5.02 hours. Full-space hydrogen-ring calculations reach 10,000 orbitals, with cyclic reduction providing further computational savings. These results show how exact reformulation, data structure exploitation and reuse of Coulomb actions make optimization of the selected large-scale SOS relaxation practical.

items.title: From Worst-Case to Smoothed Complexity in Continuous Optimization
items.summary: Worst-case complexity bounds often fail to reflect the practical performance of optimization algorithms, while average-case complexity heavily relies on the distribution of the input. In this work, we develop a smoothed-analysis framework for classical continuous optimization algorithms by studying their behaviour on random perturbations of arbitrary functions. Our main contribution is to apply methods suited for non-degenerate functions to perturbations of degenerate functions, thereby recovering the faster best-known rates for the non-degenerate class. We derive smoothed complexity guarantees for several standard methods, including (Accelerated) Gradient Descent, Conjugate Gradient, and Newton-type methods, under various settings including nonconvex ones, and show that these bounds can substantially improve upon their worst-case guarantees, bringing them closer to the practical behaviour of the respective methods.

items.title: Scattering Resonances of Plane-Embedded Cavities: A Finite Element DtN Approach
items.summary: While scattering resonances of plane-embedded cavities have wide-ranging engineering applications, numerical results for such configurations remain virtually unexplored. We present an effective finite element approach for computing these resonances. The unbounded domain is truncated using a Dirichlet-to-Neumann(DtN) boundary operator, recasting the problem as the eigenvalue problem of a holomorphic Fredholm operator function. Discretization is carried out using Lagrange finite elements with a truncated DtN expansion, and convergence is rigorously proven using Karma's approximation theory. The resulting non-linear matrix eigenvalue system is computed using a multi-step parallel spectral indicator method. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical predictions and provide benchmark solutions for future investigations.

items.title: You Can Have It All: Small sparse induced-universal graphs for minor-closed classes
items.summary: We show that, for every fixed proper minor-closed graph class $\mathcal{G}$ and every positive integer $n$, there exists a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1+o(1)}$ vertices and edges such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of $U_n$. This result generalizes and unifies the results of Dujmović et al. (J. ACM 2021) on induced-universal graphs and the results of Esperet, Joret, and Morin (J. London Math. Soc. 2023) on sparse induced-universal graphs from planar graphs to all proper minor-closed graph classes. It simultaneously improves the previous bounds for the number of vertices in induced-universal graphs (previously $O(n^2)$ obtained as a corollary of a result of DeVos et al. (J. Comb. Theory, Ser. {B} 2004) and a result of Gavoille and Labourel (ESA 2007)) and the number of edges in subgraph-universal graphs (previously $O(n^{3/2})$ by Babai et al. (Theory and Practice of Combinatorics 1982)).

items.title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
items.summary: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.

items.title: Numerical investigation of a MST conjecture for random Haar matrices
items.summary: The state-to-state control time of finite-dimensional conservative bilinear quantum systems is bounded by the weight of minimum spanning trees (MST) derived from the drift matrices. For a spectrum scaling as k^3/2 , determining whether the control time vanishes as the dimension d tends to infinity remains an open problem due to the global correlations imposed by the Haar measure. We formulate two conjectures regarding the asymptotic behavior of the MST weight\,: a general decay to zero, and a scaling in 1/sqrt(ln d) derived from an independent Gaussian surrogate model. Numerical investigations up to dimension d = 18101 validate the general decay, confirm that the exact Haar model and the independent surrogate are statistically indistinguishable in mean at all tested dimensions, and extract the thermodynamic limit $α$ = 10/3, which both models approach from below once the scaling variable 1/ ln d is adopted.

items.title: A posteriori error estimates for higher-order BDF methods for parabolic partial differential equations
items.summary: We derive a posteriori error estimates for parabolic problems discretized by conforming finite elements in space and by the backward differentiation formula of order $k$ in time, with variable step-sizes for $k \le 3$ and constant step-size for $k = 4$. The key ingredient of the analysis is a polynomial $(k+1)$-point time reconstruction of degree $k$ of the approximate solution combined with the elliptic reconstruction. We conclude upper a posteriori error bounds in $L^\infty(L^2) \cap L^2(H^1)$ and in $L^\infty(H^1) \cap H^1(L^2)$. Numerical experiments for $k = 1, \dots, 4$ with linear and quadratic finite elements confirm the optimal orders of the estimators in time and in space.

items.title: Sharp Proximity Bounds for Integer Programs with Few Rows
items.summary: We study the proximity between an optimal vertex of a standard form linear program with constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}$ and an optimal integer solution. When $m = 2$, we prove the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ-1$, where $Δ$ is the largest absolute maximal minor of $A$. When $m = 1$, we express the difference between an optimal LP vertex and an optimal integer solution as a nonnegative combination of certain generators in the kernel of $A$ with a bounded coefficient sum. This implies sharp proximity bounds for all norms when $m=1$. Combining this representation with its known counterpart for Hilbert bases due to Sissokho, we develop techniques that transfer results from $m=1$ to $m=2$. Along the way, for $m=2$, we prove that such a representation exists for an extended Gomory group relaxation and obtain the sharp infinity-norm bound $Δ$ for Graver basis elements. We also present a new short proof of Sissokho's result and lower bounds on the proximity for all $m$ and $Δ$.

items.title: Mixed-integer dual network problems are solvable in strongly polynomial time
items.summary: In this paper we show that mixed-integer linear programming is solvable in strongly polynomial time if the constraint matrix is totally unimodular with at most two nonzero entries in every row. This is done by reducing the problem to an instance of minimization of an $L$-convex function.

items.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
items.summary: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data remain distributed, moved between slab layouts using collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a p-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-pMG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for the generalised Poisson problem on octree meshes across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. These results provide practical guidelines for solver selection based on mesh structure and coefficient characteristics.

items.title: Safe and Scalable Minimax Adaptive Control of Positive Systems
items.summary: This paper studies minimax adaptive control of positive linear systems with fixed unknown dynamics and nonnegative disturbances. We reformulate the problem by compressing the historical data into a vector and a positivity-induced consistency set containing the models compatible with the observations. Together with the physical state, these quantities form a sufficient information state and yield an exact reformulation as a standard minimax dynamic game. We allow the admissible input set to adapt to the current consistency set, ensuring positivity for every remaining feasible model. As inconsistent models are eliminated, the input set can expand, allowing less cautious control actions. For finite model sets, we derive an explicit solution to the Bellman inequality and construct a safe and stabilizing certainty-equivalence controller with robustness guarantees. The framework also accommodates structured classes of continuum model uncertainty whose consistency sets admit fixed, finite-dimensional representations, enabling scalable information-state updates.

items.title: Communication-Learning Co-Design for Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
items.summary: Wireless federated learning (FL) suffers from two coupled bottlenecks: statistical heterogeneity across clients and communication-constrained model synchronization over unreliable wireless links. Instead of focusing on algorithmic design and/or wireless resource optimization, this paper provides a systematic study of pinching antenna (PA)-empowered FL for heterogeneous wireless networks and develops a unified communication-and-learning framework. Specifically, we integrate a segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (SWAN) architecture with a heterogeneity-robust FL algorithm based on client variance reduction and dual quantization, so as to jointly mitigate communication bottlenecks and client drift. On this basis, we further develop a two-stage SWAN-assisted downlink protocol and formulate fairness-oriented uplink optimization problems for PA positioning, bandwidth allocation, and quantization design. Efficient solution frameworks are then derived for the resulting downlink and uplink optimization problems. Experimental results show the superiority of the proposed design in convergence speed and final accuracy under non-independent and identically distributed data and communication bottlenecks.

items.title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
items.summary: Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.

items.title: Bounded Weighted Edit Distance with Metric Costs
items.summary: We give a deterministic $O(n+k^2)$-time algorithm for bounded weighted edit distance when the input costs form an integer metric on the alphabet extended by a gap symbol. Here $n$ is the total input length and $k$ is the given threshold on the distance. If the distance is at most $k$, the algorithm returns it with an optimal alignment. Otherwise, it reports that the distance exceeds $k$. The running time matches the classical unit-cost bound and is independent of the alphabet size and of the largest cost. The algorithm keeps only the farthest-reaching prefix alignment for each cost and each difference between the total gap costs of the aligned prefixes. For real metrics whose nonzero costs are at least one, scaling and upward rounding give a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for the bounded problem in $\widetilde{O}(n+(k/\varepsilon)^2)$ time. If insertions and deletions have integer costs, the running time improves to $\widetilde{O}(n+k^2/\varepsilon)$.

items.title: What to Predict for Efficient Scheduling on Parallel Machines
items.summary: We study learning-augmented algorithms for scheduling on multiple parallel machines under the objectives of minimizing the makespan or the total weighted completion time. We assume that the algorithm has access to noisy information (the prediction) about an optimal solution, expressed through a solution encoding that implicitly quantifies both the amount of information provided and the nature of noise (errors in the prediction). Our central question is to determine the maximum level of noise that still allows for efficiently recovering this optimal solution. We observe that information guiding greedy scheduling to optimality or revealing the optimal assignment of tasks to machines is very sensitive to noise, and prove that recovering an optimal solution from solution encodings capturing either is computationally hard, even for a small (non-constant) number of errors. On the positive side, we show that an order-based encoding, which leads to errors that are dispersed locally, is robust to noise. We present a dynamic programming framework that utilizes this encoding and solves optimally several classical scheduling problems, including makespan and total weighted completion time minimization on identical or unrelated machines.

items.title: Euclidean and Hermitian Self-Orthogonal Codes from Divisible Codes
items.summary: Self-orthogonality and divisibility are two fundamental properties of linear codes, and the relationship between them has long been of interest. Huffman and Pless (2003) showed that every binary \(4\)-divisible code is Euclidean self-orthogonal, that a ternary code is Euclidean self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(3\)-divisible, and that a quaternary code is Hermitian self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(2\)-divisible. The general case remained open for a long time. In 2024, Li and Heng settled the odd-characteristic case, proving that every \(p\)-divisible code over \(\F_{p^m}\), with \(p\) odd, that contains the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. In this paper we treat the even-characteristic case: we prove that every \(4\)-divisible code over \(\F_{2^m}\) containing the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. We also prove that, for every prime \(p\), every \(p\)-divisible linear code over \(\F_{q^2}\), where \(q=p^m\), that contains the all-one vector is Hermitian self-orthogonal. In addition, we generalize the Hermitian criterion to the Galois self-orthogonal case, proving that any $p$-divisible linear code over $\gf_{q^r}$ that contains the all-one vector is $\ell$-Galois self-orthogonal for \(\ell\in\{1,\dots,r-1\}\). These criteria make the construction of self-orthogonal codes from divisible codes simple and efficient. As applications, we recover the known Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonality of generalized Reed--Muller codes and obtain several infinite families of new Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonal codes, which give rise to infinite families of quantum codes with excellent parameters.

items.title: Real-Time String Indexing in Optimal Time
items.summary: In this paper we describe the first fully real-time indexing solution for pattern matching over an arbitrary integer alphabet. Our data structure spends $O(1)$ worst-case time w.h.p. for processing each new letter appended to $T$ and worst-case $O(|P|+occ)$ time for reporting all occurrences of $P$, where $T$ and $P$ are strings over an integer alphabet. The main idea of our solution is a novel representation of the suffix tree, the path-decomposed suffix tree, which does not store the full topology of the suffix tree but instead decomposes it into paths, each stored in a dictionary that encodes parent--child relationships indirectly.

items.title: Lengthscale Estimation for the Gaussian Kernel and Deterministic Response Functions
items.summary: The uncertainty estimates Gaussian processes output rely on the chosen covariance kernel and its hyperparameters. We study the fixed-domain asymptotics of the maximum likelihood and cross-validation estimators of the lengthscale parameter of the popular infinitely smooth Gaussian kernel when the observations are produced by a fixed univariate response function. No theoretical results for Gaussian lengthscale estimation exist in this setting. We prove lower bounds on the lengthscale estimators that depend on the regularity of the response function, as measured by the rate of decay of its Fourier transform. If the response function lives in the Hilbert space of the Gaussian kernel with lengthscale $\ell$, the lower bounds have a straightforward dependency on $\ell$. For bandlimited functions and functions whose Fourier transforms decay as $\exp(-a \lvert ω\rvert^γ)$ for $a > 0$ and $γ> 2$, we prove that the estimators blow up essentially at least as fast as $(\log n)^{(γ-2)/(2γ)}$ in the number of data points, $n$. Bandlimited functions are identified with $γ= \infty$. Unlike analogous results for finitely smooth Matérn kernels, our results make no assumptions on the geometry of the observation points. Numerical experiments illustrate the results.

items.title: N -phase flow simulations using X-Mesh and an explicit marker interface representation
items.summary: We present a marker-based X-Mesh framework for incompressible N-phase flow simulations with sharp, explicitly tracked interfaces. The interface is represented by Lagrangian marker chains, while the computational mesh is deformed so that selected mesh edges conform to the tracked geometry without changing mesh connectivity. This combination preserves the advantages of body-fitted finite element discretizations while allowing highly distorted and nearly degenerated elements to capture fine interfacial features on relatively coarse meshes without requiring mesh refinement. The arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) finite element solver uses a pressure field that is continuous within each phase and discontinuous across the fitted interface. Surface tension is introduced through a variational membrane, so the pressure jump is resolved without prescribing a curvature-dependent correction; a Young wall energy provides the corresponding treatment of fluid-fluid-solid triple points. Topological changes are handled geometrically from the marker representation. Numerical experiments illustrate the ability of the approach to transport complex interfaces and to control topology changes through marker-based feature-size criteria.

items.title: Feedback Vertex Set, Max Cut, and Edge Coloring on the Strong Product of a Graph and a Path
items.summary: We examine the computational complexity of well-known problems on subgraphs of the strong product of two paths. Namely, for Max Cut we show NP-hardness on induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ answering a question by Dvořák, Huynh, Joret, Liu, and Wood (2021). For 3-Edge Coloring we show NP-hardness on subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ and that it is equivalent to 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs for induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$. It is a long standing open question whether 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs is NP-hard. As a second contribution, we consider graphs of the form $G \boxtimes P$ and show that Feedback Vertex Set on these graphs is FPT in the clique-width of $G$. Furthermore, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is chordal or co-comparable and that the computational complexity depends on the parity of $P$ if $G$ is bipartite. Namely, it is solvable in polynomial time if $P$ has an even number of vertices but is NP-complete otherwise. For Max Cut, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is bipartite.

items.title: An Accelerated Dynamic Stochastic Primal-Dual Method for Multi-stage Stochastic Optimization
items.summary: We consider multi-stage stochastic optimization problems with smooth convex stage costs and linear linking constraints. Dynamic stochastic approximation (DSA), a stochastic first-order method, uses a recursive structure whose memory requirement grows only linearly with the number of stages. Its implementation, however, requires an exact solution of the proximal subproblem associated with the stage cost, and this subproblem often admits no closed-form solution. To resolve this issue, we develop an accelerated dynamic stochastic primal-dual (A-DSPD) framework that retains the recursive value-function structure and only requires the gradient of the stage cost. Within this framework, each stagewise saddle-point subproblem is solved by an inexact accelerated stochastic primal-dual method (iASPD), which applies Nesterov acceleration to the smooth stage cost and uses recursively generated stochastic $ε$-subgradients for the nonsmooth downstream value function. For the stochastic composite saddle-point problem, after $N$ primal-dual updates, iASPD yields optimality and feasibility bounds in which the contribution of the smooth stage cost decays at a faster rate $O(1/N^2)$, while the terms associated with stochastic $ε$-subgradients of the nonsmooth value function decay as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$, up to the prescribed oracle inexactness. We also develop bounds for the stochastic $ε$-subgradient estimators and the dual iterates, which yield complexity guarantees for A-DSPD. Specifically, A-DSPD computes an $ε$-solution using $O(1/ε^4)$ sampled scenarios and $O(1/ε^5)$ primal-dual updates for three-stage problems. We further extend the method and its convergence analysis to problems with an arbitrary finite number of stages. Numerical experiments on three-stage stochastic portfolio models illustrate the empirical advantage of the proposed method.

items.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_σ$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $σ$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $Ω=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a Hölder Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $μ\in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (μ)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $σ$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(μ)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(μ)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_σ$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:Ω\to \mathbb{R}$. $μ\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(ρ|| ν)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.

items.title: LongTails: Automated Research in Optimization
items.summary: We introduce LongTails, a framework for discovering and improving oracle-complexity bounds with formal verification in Lean 4. Using LongTails, we have already obtained more than 100 new results across a broad range of optimization problems, including generalized smoothness, heavy-tailed noise, finite-sum and composite optimization, and higher-order and zeroth-order methods. Our goal is to scale discovery and continually develop new methods with non-trivial and valuable theoretical guarantees using modern agentic systems. The framework is specialized for optimization, where we separate a Setup, specifying the problem class, assumptions, available information, and success criterion, from a Complexity, specifying a sufficient oracle-call budget. Once a Setup is fixed (e.g., $L$-smooth convex optimization with the goal of finding $x_{\mathrm{out}}$ such that $f(x_{\mathrm{out}}) - f(x^\star) \leq \varepsilon$), agents search for better Complexities (e.g., $O(\sqrt{L R^2 / \varepsilon})$, where $R \geq \|x_0 - x^\star\|$) by designing algorithms and proving their convergence. The framework then checks the proofs and guarantees that every accepted Complexity can indeed be attained under the given Setup. This turns the search for new methods into an ongoing effort to improve their theoretical guarantees. To the best of our knowledge, LongTails is the first framework to scale automated research in optimization across such a broad range of problems with formally verified theoretical guarantees.

items.title: Online Network Design with Maximum Delay and Stochastic Arrivals
items.summary: We study online network services that combine pending requests into batches. Each batch pays for its spatial service and for the waiting time of its oldest request. The objective is the sum of these costs over all batches. Thus requests can share both a spatial purchase and one maximum-delay charge. We assume independent Poisson arrivals of known rates, while actual requests are revealed only upon arrival. For stateless services, suppose that each type has an attainable minimum cost when served alone, that every batch costs at least the stand-alone minimum of each type it contains, and that one finite-cost action can serve any batch, regardless of its request multiplicities. We give a deterministic algorithm with long-run ratio of expectations $e/(e-1)$ against an unrestricted offline optimum. This factor is optimal, even allowing randomization, already at one request location. The key comparison measures the union of time intervals associated with requests. The theorem applies directly to multi-root and pair aggregation on trees. We also study facility location, where each request pays its own connection distance and the bounded-action assumption can fail. A deterministic policy gives a ratio $3$ for arbitrary nonnegative opening costs. It immediately serves a finite initial set of requests, computes an assignment from their observed arrival gaps, and then keeps that assignment fixed. Its analysis combines Poisson insertion with a time-slice packing bound on the offline optimum. Every guarantee includes the full cost of completing finite inputs without an end-of-input signal.

items.title: Online Network Design with Additive Delays and Poisson Arrivals
items.summary: We study online service systems in which requests arrive at locations in a network. A service may open a facility and connect customers, buy a subtree linking them to a root, or send a mobile server to visit them. Combining requests can save opening, network, or travel costs, but each request pays its own waiting time. The objective is the sum of these spatial costs and individual delays. We assume independent Poisson arrivals of known rates. The algorithms know how often requests occur, but observe them only upon arrival. We show that these rates suffice to make fixed spatial choices that compete with an offline optimum free to adapt to the realized input. We obtain long-run ratios of expectations below $27.249$ for facility location in finite metrics, $94.415$ for multi-root aggregation on trees, and $24.326$ for online service on trees. All three algorithms are deterministic; the multi-root algorithm also has polynomial-time preprocessing on rational inputs. The proofs connect rate-based spatial choices with lower bounds on unavoidable purchase, movement, and waiting costs. All main proofs are self-contained, and every guarantee includes the full cost of completing finite inputs.

items.title: Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Exit Games with Singular Belief Dynamics
items.summary: We study a two-player nonzero-sum stochastic exit game with asymmetric information. Each firm chooses the time to exit a duopoly and, conditional on remaining active, when to exit a monopoly. The asymmetry stems from privately observed exit values, while profit flows are driven by a general one-dimensional diffusion. Allowing for exit from monopoly induces singular dynamics of the associated belief process, so we construct it as a limit of regular approximations. The underlying dynamics are not described by a system of SDEs, which requires a new mathematical approach. We construct a symmetric Nash equilibrium in which the duopoly exit is a hitting time of the belief process while the monopoly exit is described through the underlying diffusion. Our equilibrium exhibits novel phenomena: the market may be abandoned by both firms in finite time (market collapse), and firms with heterogeneous exit values may optimally exit simultaneously (clustering). These features are absent when monopoly is always preferred to exit.

items.title: Learning the Brownian Motion in Machine Learning for Parametric Parabolic PDEs: A Backward Quadrature Approach
items.summary: We propose a backward quadrature learning (BQL) method for solving high dimensional parametric semilinear parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs). To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to extend the applicability of BSDE-based stochastic numerical methods to this class of PDEs. Specifically, inspired by the approach of learning the random variables (LRV)~\cite{BeckerJentzenMullerWurstemberger2024}, BQL incorporates learnable quadrature for Brownian increments at each time level into the backward recursion of BSDEs, enabling more efficient layerwise approximation of local conditional expectations. Furthermore, BQL introduces a continuation surrogate to facilitate the transfer of value-function information from subsequent to preceding time levels, avoiding nested quadrature while controlling the propagation of local approximation errors. Our main theoretical contribution is the derivation of a global error bound that explicitly characterizes the decomposition of the total error, together with a proof of first-order mean-square convergence under suitable approximation and integrability assumptions. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate that BQL achieves competitive solution accuracy while substantially reducing the amortized computational cost per query. For the HJB benchmark across the tested dimensions, with $Q=7$ parameter queries, BQL achieves computational cost reductions of approximately 40-fold and 4-fold compared with P$^2$INN~[2] and FBSNN~[3], respectively.

items.title: Local Modifications of Nearest-Neighbor and Min-Plus Representations
items.summary: We study how changing a Boolean-valued function at $d$ inputs affects the size and precision of its exact representations. Starting from a representation of size $m$, we prove four bounds, two for nearest-neighbor (NN) representations and two for integer min-plus representations. (i) For NN representations on a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$, at most $m+2d$ anchors suffice. The coefficient $2$ is optimal: on a three-point domain, changing one value can increase the minimum number of anchors from one to three. (ii) For NN representations on the Boolean cube with rational anchors, let $R$ be the maximum original coordinate bit length, and let $Δ$ be the maximum bit length of the least common denominator of any one original anchor's coordinates. We construct a representation with at most $m+3d$ anchors on a common dyadic grid and coordinate bit length $O(R+Δ+\log(n+1))$. (iii) For integer min-plus representations on the Boolean cube, we give a construction that keeps the original $m$ forms and their labels and adds at most $d$ new forms. Its maximum weight is at most $W+2n$, where $W$ is the largest absolute original coefficient, including constant terms. (iv) For integer min-plus representations on a finite rational domain $X\subset\mathbb{Q}^n$, at most $m+2d$ forms suffice. Their maximum weight is polynomially bounded in $m,d,W,n,|X|$, the coordinate bound, and the common denominator of $X$. The coefficient $2$ is again optimal: on a three-point domain, changing one value can increase the minimum number of forms from one to three. These bounds imply stability under polynomially many changes on the cube for polynomial-size representations, including those with polynomially bounded NN coordinate bit length or min-plus weight.

items.title: Unified Far-field and Near-field Codebook Design for XL-array Systems
items.summary: While extremely large-scale antenna arrays (XL-arrays) hold immense promise for next-generation wireless networks, the paradigm shift encompassing new near-field communications renders conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based Type-I codebooks inefficient. Meanwhile, existing near-field alternatives usually impose prohibitively high storage and/or feedback burdens. To tackle these challenges, we propose in this letter a unified codebook applicable to both far-field and near-field XL-array systems. Our key idea is to express the near-field channel steering vector in an equivalent form, which is a Hadamard product of an angular vector and a curvature-related vector. This new representation allows direct reuse of the legacy Type-I codebook for angle quantization, while only a lightweight auxiliary codebook is newly added for additional curvature quantization. Subsequently, we optimize the auxiliary curvature codebook by maximizing the average beamforming gain given the information of user distribution. By leveraging the local monotonicity of the beamforming gain with respect to curvature mismatch, the optimization problem is further reduced to a quantization-error minimization problem, for which suboptimal curvature codewords are obtained. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed unified codebook achieves near-optimal beamforming performance that approaches its upper bound based on perfect channel state information (CSI), while significantly reducing the required feedback overhead as compared to various benchmark schemes.

items.title: Stochastic Aggregation with Prescribed Resources and Additive Delay
items.summary: We study online aggregation with prescribed resources and additive delay. In this problem, we are given a finite set of resources with purchase costs and a collection of request types, each specifying the resources it requires. Requests arrive over time, and each request can be served immediately or postponed to a later time. A service may serve several pending requests together by purchasing every resource required by at least one of them, paying for each purchased resource only once. These purchases serve only the current batch; resources needed in a later service must be purchased again. A request served $t$ units of time after its arrival incurs delay cost $t$. The objective is to serve all requests while minimizing the sum of resource purchase costs and individual delay costs. We consider a stochastic version of this problem in which requests of each type follow an independent Poisson process of known rate. An online algorithm knows these rates but observes requests only upon arrival. We compare its expected cost with that of an offline optimum that knows the entire realized input and may choose every batch freely. A resource--scale linear program supplies both an offline lower certificate and synchronized service periods. This yields a deterministic online algorithm with polynomial-time preprocessing on rational input and a long-run ratio of expectations below $2.113$. The guarantee applies in particular to rooted multi-level aggregation and prescribed-pair aggregation on trees. Besides, for Poisson TCP acknowledgment, we further characterize the optimal long-run ratio of expectations at every load, showing that its worst-case value is approximately 1.409 and is attained by a deterministic online policy.

items.title: List Update with Per-Page Maximum Delay
items.summary: We study list update with per-page maximum delay. Requests may wait, and one access clears all pending requests of a page at its current list rank, paying their maximum waiting penalty. Each service can change the permutation and therefore the cost of later accesses. We give a strictly $5$-competitive deterministic algorithm: serve a page when the oldest waiting time reaches two thirds of its current rank, then move it to the front. Our main tool is an asynchronous marked-rank coupling that compares different list orders and different service histories. A temporal transfer principle separates this permutation argument from two waiting-cost inequalities. It gives factor $5$ for page-specific superadditive penalties, common calendar rates, and additional hard deadlines; deadlines alone admit factor $3$. Two structural conditions on request-specific penalties give factor $3+2κ$. In particular, nonincreasing request severity retains factor $5$ even with unbounded weight ratios. For linear delay, offline optimization is NP-complete but fixed-parameter tractable in the number of pages. We characterize fixed-list batching, show an $Ω(m)$ gap between the best static order and dynamic reordering, and prove that the optimal deterministic factor for one page is exactly $2$. Counterexamples delineate the threshold rule's scope.

items.title: Decision-Focused Learning via Neural Optimization Layers for Battery-Assisted Grid-Import Smoothing in AI Data Centers
items.summary: Rapid AI data-center power fluctuations challenge grid integration. Sustained grid-import smoothing requires allocating limited battery power and energy under uncertain demand. We formulate risk-aware BESS scheduling that coordinates advance reserve commitments and demand-responsive dispatch, accounting for operating costs, grid-ramp penalties, and their conditional value-at-risk. We develop battery scheduling decision-focused learning (BS-DFL) with a constraint-aware neural optimization layer trained directly from this objective without optimal-solution labels. The trained layer is then frozen to guide demand-predictor learning through scheduling costs and ramping risk, enabling solver-free rolling-horizon scheduling. In a 10,000-minute simulation using loads derived from measured AI workloads, BS-DFL reduces mean absolute minute-to-minute grid-import changes by 71.70% and total scheduling cost by 18.01% relative to an MSE-trained predictor coupled with a mixed-integer linear programming solver, with an average decision time of 18.77 ms.

items.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
items.summary: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

items.title: Proximal gradient method for multiobjective interval valued optimization problem with application in portfolio selection
items.summary: In this article, we consider a class of unconstrained multiobjective interval-valued optimization problems in which each objective function is a sum of a generalized Hukuhara(gH)-differentiable interval valued function and a proper, convex and gH-lower semicontinuous interval valued function, which is possibly non-gH-differentiable. Within this framework, we introduce the notion of a proximal gradient direction and characterize the Pareto critical points of the considered problem through a strongly convex auxiliary subproblem. Based on these characterizations, we develop a proximal gradient algorithm with an Armijo-type line search that ensures sufficient descent with respect to the interval partial order. We then establish the existence of an uniform lower bound on the admissible step length, the global convergence of the generated sequence to a Pareto critical point followed by a global rate of convergence in the general nonconvex setting. The theoretical findings of the proposed method are validated through some test problems and further illustrate its applicability on portfolio selection problems involving interval-valued data.

items.title: Proximal point algorithm for interval valued optimization problems with application to lasso problem
items.summary: In this paper, we consider a class of unconstrained interval valued optimization problems and using a suitable scalarization technique, we formulate an associated scalarized optimization problem and establish the relationships between the optimal solution of the scalarized problem and the $LU$-nondominated solution of the considered optimization problem. Based on this framework, we propose a proximal point algorithm and derive the global convergence of the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm along with the sublinear and linear rate of convergence for convex and strongly convex cases, respectively. Finally, we provide suitable numerical experiments along with comparative analysis with an existing method and applicability of the proposed algorithm on an interval valued lasso regression problem, highlighting its potential in machine learning models with uncertain data.

items.title: Robustness of controllability scores for stable linear network systems
items.summary: Controllability scores quantify node importance in linear network systems by optimizing the allocation of input strength. Although the volumetric controllability score (VCS) and average-energy controllability score (AECS) are uniquely defined for Hurwitz systems, their sensitivity to perturbations of the system matrix remains unclear. In this paper, we investigate the robustness of these scores to such perturbations. We first prove that both scores are locally Lipschitz continuous in the system matrix and establish a robustness bound for Hurwitz comparison matrices. We then characterize the directional derivative of the optimal allocation along a differentiable matrix path as the unique solution of a critical-cone quadratic program, whose linear term is computed using differentiated Lyapunov equations. For single-edge weakening, the norm of the resulting response vector provides a robustness-based measure of edge importance. Numerical experiments show that the response, and hence the edge importance, depends on both the criterion and the dynamics, not only on the network topology.

items.title: Min-CSPs on Complete Instances III: Nearly Optimal Characterizations of Approximation for Symmetric CSPs
items.summary: This paper studies complete Min-$k$-CSPs: an instance on $n$ variables has one nontrivial constraint for every $k$-set of variables (so $\binom{n}{k}$ constraints in total), and the goal is to find an assignment that minimizes the number of unsatisfied constraints. They are motivated by the connections to machine learning and data science, as well as the possibility of being testbeds for new algorithmic techniques. Previous recent results presented polynomial-time algorithms for the decision version of every complete Boolean $k$-CSP, which is a necessary condition for any multiplicative approximations for the minimization version, but nontrivial approximation results have been limited to fragile CSPs, 2-SAT, and NAE-3-SAT, leaving the approximability of most complete Boolean Min-CSPs open, including complete Min-$k$-SAT. In this paper, we resolve this question, up to nearly matching factors, for the natural class of symmetric Boolean predicates. Given $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, k\}$, Min-CSP($A$) is a Min-$k$-CSP where each constraint is specified by $k$ literals and is satisfied if the number of true literals belongs to $A$. Let $w(A)$ be the maximum number of consecutive integers in $A$. Our main results for complete Min-CSP($A$) are (1) a QPTAS for $w(A) \leq 2$ and (2) an $\widetilde{O}(n^{w(A)-3})$-approximation for $w(A) \geq 3$, as well as almost matching hardness results for the latter. Our QPTAS for $w(A)=2$ significantly improves the previous $O(1)$-approximation for Min-2-SAT and the $\operatorname{polylog}(n)$-approximation for Min-NAE-3-SAT, as well as extends the PTAS for fragile CSPs (i.e., $w(A) = 1$).

items.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
items.summary: Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.

items.title: Parameterized Complexity and Geometric Approximation of Riesz Energy Subset Selection
items.summary: We choose $k$ of $n$ sites to minimize Riesz $s$-energy, in which a pair at distance $t$ contributes $t^{-s}$. For $s=2$, exact selection is polynomial on a line but NP-hard in the plane. Adapting the proxy lemma of Ceccarello et al. gives an efficient parameterized approximation scheme (EPAS) for fixed Euclidean dimension and fixed $s>0$. To sharpen the bound, we start with a geometric packing. Farthest-first traversal gives $2k$ centers separated by at least the last insertion distance $r$. If one site of an optimum is removed, each of the $k-1$ remaining sites excludes at most one center closer than $r/2$, leaving at least $k+1$ centers free. The new step is a discrete exchange bound: the removed site's interaction energy is at most the average it would contribute at those free centers. In the plane at $s=2$, this reduces the representative bound from $O(k^2\log(2k)/\varepsilon^2)$ for a packing estimate of total energy to $O(k\log(2k)/\varepsilon^2)$, independently of $n$. Rational planar examples show that the resulting separation scale $r/\sqrt{\log(2k)}$ is sharp. A $(1+\varepsilon)$ approximation on rational planar sites takes $O(nk+n\log n)+(C\log(2k)/\varepsilon^2)^k$ operations of polynomial bit cost. The observed number $M$ of representatives determines the search size $\binom{M}{k}$. With one million sites, $k=5$ and $\varepsilon=1/2$, the exchange grid left 252 subsets on clustered inputs and about $9.3\times10^{26}$ on uniform inputs. The method extends to metrics of bounded doubling dimension and to compact domains with effective geometric routines, including filled simple polygons. At $s=2$, exact decision on metrics with nonzero distances in $\{1,2\}$ is W[1]-complete in $k$. A gap that shrinks with $k$ rules out a deterministic EPAS on unrestricted metrics unless FPT = W[1].

items.title: Two nodally bound-preserving and mass-conservative discontinuous Galerkin methods for reaction-diffusion problems
items.summary: We propose and analyze two high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods that preserve prescribed nodal bounds and total mass for reaction-diffusion problems with anisotropic and heterogeneous diffusion. Both methods combine a weighted interior-penalty prediction step with a convex correction in either the dG energy or the $L^2$ metric. We construct a pointwise bound-preserving and cellwise mass-preserving comparison function with optimal local approximation properties. This construction yields optimal dG-energy error estimates for the energy correction and, under a dual regularity assumption, optimal $L^2$ and dG-energy error estimates for the $L^2$ correction on quasi-uniform meshes. We further establish a general a posteriori estimate that combines a predictor estimator with the computable correction norm. The resulting estimators are globally reliable and efficient up to data oscillation, with parameter-dependent efficiency constants. Numerical experiments compare the two corrections and illustrate their use in adaptive computations.

items.title: Approximating graphic TSP by b-matchings
items.summary: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour of length at most $\frac{89}{64}=\frac{7}{5}-\frac{3}{320}$ times the value of the subtour relaxation. This improves the long-standing ratio $\frac75$ of Sebő and Vygen and shows that the integrality gap of the subtour LP on graphic instances is at most $\frac{89}{64}\approx 1.3906$. We optimize a non-linear objective function over an odd-join polytope, which uses (i) a new removable system of edges, and (ii) reconnection of subtours if the graph is disconnected. This approach gives a $\frac{13}{10}$-approximation algorithm for $4$-regular $4$-vertex-connected graphs, improving the $\frac43$ of Newman, and a $\frac43$-approximation for $k$-vertex-connected graphs of maximum degree at most $k+1$, for every $k\ge 3$. For the general graphic TSP, we construct a feasible point in the odd-join polytope, using an optimal vertex from the Subtour linear programming relaxation of TSP, which helps us bound the approximation factor by 89/64.

items.title: Exact (Non-)Accelerations of Heavy-Ball Discretizations
items.summary: Momentum methods with the same slow dynamics can have different worst-case rates on smooth strongly convex functions. We identify a half-step phase barrier in the gradient query that governs this difference. For momentum with extrapolation $τ_κ\toτ$, $β=1-θ/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$ and $hL\to y$, where $κ=L/μ$ and $θ,y>0$, the exact uniform distance factor is $1-c/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$, with $c=\min\{θ/3,c_Q(θ,y)\}$, when $τ>1/2$ and $y(1+2τ)<4$; $c_Q$ is the slowest quadratic decay exponent. Quadratically accelerated families with $\limsupτ_κ<1/2$ have divergent trajectories on the full function class. Upper bounds use finite-lag certificates: nonnegative combinations of inequalities for values and gradients at finitely separated query points, together with comparisons to the minimizer. For any prescribed accuracy, spiral mixtures or quadratic trajectories of one finite-dimensional objective give matching lower bounds at all iteration horizons. We resolve the parameter layer near $τ=1/2$ and classify all tunings of this family attaining the optimal leading constant 1. The flow also bounds the leading constant of every second-order stationary linear family with the same slow parameters $(θ,y)$ and fixed finite memory.

items.title: Greedy+Singleton for knapsack-constrained monotone submodular maximization has approximation ratio exactly $β^\star \approx 0.42944$
items.summary: Greedy+Singleton is the textbook heuristic for monotone submodular maximization under a knapsack constraint: it returns the better of the cost-benefit greedy set and the best single item. Its worst-case approximation ratio, known only to lie in $[0.427, 0.42945]$ (Feldman-Nutov-Shoham; Kulik-Schwartz-Shachnai), is exactly an explicit constant $β^\star\approx 0.42944$. In the extremal instances, many cheap "filler" items wear down the value of two large optimal items while greedy spends the budget, until neither fits. This picture gives a sharper factor-revealing relaxation; we bound it analytically near the extremal parameters, up to finitely many interval-arithmetic checks, and certify it elsewhere by an exact branch-and-bound. The matching bad instances are tie-free and checkable by hand. For the version that stops at the first item that does not fit, Wolsey's bound $1-e^{-β_W}\approx 0.35780$, where $e^{β_W}=2-β_W$, is tight; Wolsey stated this for his variant without giving the instances, and we give an explicit family with no ties that also covers comparison with the best feasible singleton. The CELF rule also has ratio exactly $β^\star$.

items.title: Third-Order Asymptotics for Fixed-Length Lossy Compression of Discrete Memoryless Sources
items.summary: This paper determines the third-order asymptotics of the logarithm of the minimum codebook size for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete memoryless sources. For an excess-distortion probability constraint $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and every interior distortion level, we establish a third-order correction of $\frac12\log n+O(1)$, where $n$ is the blocklength. This sharpens the general bounds of Kostina and Verdú [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 2012]. The main technical innovation lies in the converse for positive dispersion. Under a reverse change of measure, we retain the exponential weights associated with tilted information and distortion slack and control them jointly using the multivariate weighted-strip estimate of Scarlett, Martinez, and Guillén i Fàbregas [Proc. IEEE ISIT, 2015]. A pairing argument verifies the required covariance nondegeneracy uniformly over all reconstruction words whose distortion balls meet a typical set, yielding the matching converse.

items.title: Improved Bounds for Online Matching with Random Edge Arrivals
items.summary: We study the unweighted online matching problem with random edge arrivals, where each edge arrives at an independent time drawn uniformly from $[0,1]$, and the algorithm must immediately and irrevocably accept or reject it while maintaining a matching. Guruganesh and Singla (IPCO, 2017) first broke the $1/2$ barrier of the naive Greedy algorithm by giving a $(1/2+\varepsilon)$-competitive algorithm for a small constant $\varepsilon>0$, a guarantee that has remained the best known for nearly a decade. We give a simple three-phase algorithm that achieves a competitive ratio of $0.5445$ by deliberately rejecting selected early edges to reserve their endpoints for later matching opportunities. With a different choice of parameters, the same algorithm is $0.5535$-competitive on triangle-free graphs, including bipartite graphs. We also establish competitive ratio upper bounds below $0.6964$ for general graphs and $0.7043$ for bipartite graphs via exact rational evaluation of an optimal-policy recurrence on fixed graphs, even when the input graph is known up to isomorphism.

items.title: Pair-Merge Tokenisation Is Hard to Approximate on Binary Strings and Strongly NP-Hard on Unary Datasets
items.summary: Tokenisers such as Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) shorten text by repeatedly merging an adjacent pair of symbols into a new one; fewer tokens mean less computation. We ask whether an efficient algorithm can choose $k$ merges that leave a string of length $n$ almost as short as possible; doing nothing is already within a factor $n$. We prove that, unless P = NP, no polynomial-time algorithm comes within a factor $c\,n/\log n$, for some constant $c>0$, already for one binary string and for BPE-style merges that replace every occurrence. The key idea is that $k$ merges form a grammar with $k$ rules: a vertex-cover gap becomes a grammar-size gap, which we amplify with relabelled copies, encode in binary and realise with explicit merges. For merges that may skip occurrences, a simple algorithm achieves $O(n/\log\log n)$, and no Karp reduction can prove hardness beyond order $n/\log n$ unless coNP $\subseteq$ NP/poly. Over a one-letter alphabet, both tokenisation problems left open by Kastreva et al. are strongly NP-complete on datasets with repeated strings.

items.title: Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence
items.summary: Evaluating a learned AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) surrogate on one grid serialization cannot show whether its accuracy depends on that encoding. We test this dependence with thirteen metamorphic relations, each specifying when a transformation is valid and how to compare its outputs. Our audit covers 17 model and pipeline configurations: two released trained checkpoints and 15 random-weight architecture or mechanism controls. Every configuration violates at least six relations, even at reporting tolerances ten times tighter or looser. For GridSFM-Open v1.1, source inspection and intermediate-tensor interventions point to an indexing bug and three noncanonical or numerically unstable preprocessing choices; a repaired checkpoint remains untested. In a separate case500 training experiment, augmentation lowers transformed-view error in three of four models and median discrepancy and constraint-violation P95 in all four. These benefits depend on the training protocol: some relations worsen, and every evaluated prediction remains AC infeasible. A GPU/CPU eigensolver mismatch accounts for most of the large raw-Laplacian-baseline gain. We recommend reporting representation consistency alongside accuracy, feasibility, and cost. These results establish neither deployment readiness nor universal invariance.

items.title: Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Benders Decomposition for Security-constrained Transmission Expansion Planning
items.summary: Energy grids worldwide rely on efficient, effective and resilient transmission networks to deliver power from generators to geographically distant destinations. The optimisation problem of designing these networks is made very difficult by the non-linearity and non-convexity of the equations which govern AC power flow. In this paper we propose the Adaptive Multi-Fidelity Benders Decomposition (AMFBD) algorithm, which is capable of solving to global optimality the Security-Constrained Transmission Expansion Planning problems with N-1 redundancy, using the non-convex AC power flow equations. We demonstrate the practical capability of this algorithm by solving security-constrained expansion problems based on the Garver 6-bus problem and the 14-bus IEEE test case. Given the large costs generally associated with energy grids, globally optimal investment decisions that can be found using AMFBD have the potential to provide significant practical benefits over suboptimal solutions produced by approximations or heuristics.

items.title: A Variable-metric Inexact Progressive Hedging Algorithm with a Lagged Stopping Criterion for Multistage Stochastic Variational Inequalities
items.summary: The progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) solves multistage stochastic variational inequalities (SVIs) by independently solving regularized scenario subproblems and enforcing nonanticipativity through primal-dual updates. Since these subproblems are often solved iteratively, practical implementations need stopping criteria that control errors while preserving convergence. We propose iVMPHA-Lag, a variable-metric inexact PHA with a lagged stopping criterion for monotone SVIs. The method allows scenario block metrics to vary across outer iterations while remaining compatible with nonanticipativity. For each scenario, an error budget combines a positive fraction of the previous budget with a progress measure from the preceding outer iteration. This gives a stopping tolerance fixed before the inner iterations begin, so each scenario can check its criterion independently without a prescribed summable tolerance sequence. With positive initial budgets and a positive inexactness parameter, we prove finite inner termination provided the inner solver produces valid approximations whose residual and enlargement errors tend to zero. Under suitable conditions, we establish global convergence of the primal-dual iterates and local $R$-linear convergence under metric subregularity at the limit point. Numerical experiments on synthetic strongly monotone box-constrained SVIs show that iVMPHA-Lag with adaptive metrics uses fewer scenario evaluations and less time on average than exact PHA and the competing inexact methods among the tested configurations in all four baseline regimes. Its average time advantage over the competing inexact methods persists across the tested problem sizes. Further comparisons show that metric adaptation improves efficiency over the fixed scalar configuration, while lagged stopping and positive budget retention reduce inner computational work.

items.title: Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models
items.summary: Nonlinear state space models are typically evaluated sequentially, limiting their ability to exploit modern parallel hardware. Recent work has shown that state space models can be evaluated in parallel by reformulating evaluation as a root-finding problem, which can be solved with a parallel form of Newton's method. However, exact Newton methods require expensive multiplication of dense Jacobian matrices, and quasi-Newton methods based on diagonal approximations, while more scalable, are often slow to converge because they neglect interactions across state dimensions. We introduce a novel quasi-Newton approach based on Broyden's method, which captures coupling terms with diagonal-plus-low-rank approximations to blocks of the Jacobian. We construct the approximations from trajectory secants, avoiding automatic differentiation while retaining the favorable scaling of diagonal approximations and remaining compatible with parallel scan through rank compression. We prove finite-step recovery of the exact trajectory under the compressed scan, and show that convergence is tracked by the compression error and by the block approximation error along the current trajectory error, rather than in spectral norm. Empirically, we show that our method is advantageous when interactions are approximately low rank or when Jacobian evaluation is expensive: on low-rank RNNs, parallel MCMC algorithms, and denoising diffusion models, it converges in fewer iterations than other quasi-Newton methods and is the fastest parallel method when Jacobian evaluation is expensive or state dimensions are large.

items.title: A Fast Proximal-Gradient Algorithm for Decentralised Optimisation
items.summary: We consider a connected multi-agent network where agents coordinate to minimise a finite sum of convex functions. Each function in the sum can be further expressed as the sum of a smooth and nonsmooth component and is known only to a single agent in the network. We propose a decentralised proximal-gradient-type algorithm for solving this problem, which we term Fast PG-EXTRA. In each iteration, agents evaluate the gradient of the smooth component of their local objective functions and the proximal operator of the nonsmooth component, followed by communicating the results with neighbouring agents in the network. Fast PG-EXTRA can be viewed as an accelerated variant of PG-EXTRA, in the sense that it enjoys non-ergodic $o(1/k^2)$ convergence rates in terms of the first-order optimality residual, successive iterates, and consensus error, compared to PG-EXTRA's ergodic $O(1/k)$ convergence rates. Our analysis of Fast PG-EXTRA is based on an accelerated variant of the Condat--Vũ algorithm for non-distributed convex minimisation, which has similarly improved convergence rates compared to the Condat--Vũ algorithm. We validate our convergence results for Fast PG-EXTRA and demonstrate its potential advantages compared to PG-EXTRA with numerical experiments for power state system estimation and $l_1$-regularised logistic regression.

items.title: Multiscale LegONet: Learning Coefficient-Dependent Local Spaces for Composable Multiscale Finite Elements with Localized Error Bounds
items.summary: We introduce multiscale LegONet (Ms-LegONet), a plug-and-play learned block for heterogeneous elliptic problems. One network per spatial dimension is trained once on local coefficient patches and reused, without retraining, across coefficient layouts, sources, boundary data and domain sizes within the trained coefficient class. On a fixed primitive patch the network maps the local coefficient to a zero-boundary space, the only learned object.
